software-feature-contracts.premise: The response changed order while the fitted coefficients stayed put.

construction.title: Repair the model input boundary
construction.start: Build a name-to-position branch, gather the readings, and connect the coefficients last.
construction.outcome: A transport change no longer changes feature meaning.
hints: A coefficient belongs to a named measurement. First find the incoming position of each name in the model’s required order.
Gather values using those positions before the dot product. Rearranging the weights to follow an unverified response would move the contract into the wrong place.

investigation.title: The response arrives backwards
investigation.question: The values reverse with their names. Should the prediction change?
investigation.outcome: Try the metadata field without assigning it a weight.

options.label: No; gather according to the saved schema
options.feedback: The model sees the same temperature and vibration after the adapter.

options.label: Yes; coefficients follow incoming positions
options.feedback: Those positions belong to the transport format, not the trained model.

connections.why: The array now has an external schema whose meaning must survive reordering.

reflection.prompt: What should happen if temperature changes units?
reflection.carryForward: Store units and order with the fitted artifact.

software-fitted-state.premise: An extreme neighbour changes a reading that the model already knew how to process.

construction.title: Separate training from serving
construction.start: Connect the training mean to the reference input, then route all request values through subtraction.
construction.outcome: The model reference survives a change in request grouping.
hints: The reference comes from the training readings. A new request must not help set the mean used to judge itself.
Calculate the training mean on one branch and share it across the request values. An extreme neighbouring request should not move that reference.

investigation.title: Another request joins the batch
investigation.question: The second request is 100. What should happen to the centred value for 7?
investigation.outcome: Compare the first entry across both runs; it must stay 3.

connections.why: After preserving names, we preserve the fitted reference those names depend on.

reflection.prompt: Which attributes would a scaler need beyond this mean?
reflection.carryForward: Save every learned preprocessing value with the model version.

software-retrieval-shortlists.premise: A sorted score list is useless if Botie can no longer find its passages.

construction.title: Preserve identities through ranking
construction.start: Rank the score positions, then use them to gather IDs without sorting the ID list.
construction.outcome: Each selected ID still belongs to the score that earned its position.
hints: Keep the scores attached to their record IDs. Sorting scores alone loses which record each score described.
Find positions in descending score order, then gather IDs with those same positions. Equal scores retain their incoming order.

investigation.title: Two manuals tie for the remaining slots
investigation.question: Which IDs survive when B and C both score 0.9?
investigation.outcome: Keep B before C according to the declared stable tie rule.

connections.why: The same gather operation now follows ranked evidence rather than a feature schema.

reflection.prompt: Which test would expose a mismatch between IDs and scores?
reflection.carryForward: Keep record identity attached through every sorting and filtering step.

software-workflow-dependencies.premise: A job consumed stale features because the scheduler confused an existing file with this run’s completion.

construction.title: Calculate readiness from the declared graph
construction.start: Count completed dependencies separately for each waiting job and compare with its required count.
construction.outcome: Unrelated completions cannot release a dependent task.
hints: Each matrix row names one waiting job’s prerequisites. An unrelated completed job cannot satisfy that row.
Count completed prerequisites per row and compare with that row’s required count. A row requiring none is ready even when no earlier work has finished.

investigation.title: Fitting finishes without the required preparation
investigation.question: The completion vector is [0,1]. May either of these waiting rows run?
investigation.outcome: Complete both prerequisites and verify that both rows become ready.

options.label: Neither; both require the first prerequisite
options.feedback: The first column is still incomplete in every row.

options.label: Both; one finished job is enough
options.feedback: Each row names its own requirements rather than a global count.

connections.skill: Assign state to the correct lifetime
connections.why: The fitted object now belongs to a run whose inputs must be ready before construction.

reflection.prompt: What identifies the exact feature artifact a fitting task consumed?
reflection.carryForward: Record run identity and artifact identity beside completion status.

software-named-request-contracts.premise: A truthiness shortcut made a valid zero disappear.

construction.title: Inspect what the caller supplied
construction.start: Place the field inspector first, then split its result into a decision branch and a numerical-value branch.
construction.outcome: A missing key can use a default without accepting a null or replacing zero.
hints: Follow the inspection result into both branches so their positions stay aligned.
The action branch names the policy. The resolver uses the fallback only when the inspector says missing.

investigation.title: The old shortcut sees four false-looking inputs
investigation.question: The changed case contains zero, null, text "0" and an absent field. Which distinction must the repaired construction preserve?
investigation.outcome: Test the original requests again after adding the missing/null distinction.

options.label: Only the absent field uses the default
options.feedback: A zero is numerical data. Null and text are supplied values that this contract rejects.

options.label: Every unusual value becomes the default
options.feedback: That would conceal a producer error and overwrite real zeroes.

connections.skill: Keep a measurement attached to its name
connections.why: Before ordering fields, decide whether each named value is admissible.

reflection.prompt: What would change if the model had been trained with a distinct missing-value indicator?
reflection.carryForward: Write the missing/null policy beside the fitted model, rather than inferring it from truthiness.

preparation.title: See the three field states before choosing a policy
preparation.challenge: Connect requests and the field name to the inspector. Read how an absent key differs from a supplied null.
preparation.why: Inspection preserves evidence before a default can erase the distinction.
hints: The inspector needs the entire record, not only the result of get.
A present zero should have kind number.

software-schema-evolution.premise: The old parser worked until a supported caller selected the new shape.

construction.title: Build the two public edges around one internal form
construction.start: Place both adapters and connect their results to the matching version-selection ports.
construction.outcome: The internal search record stays stable while the public keys differ.
hints: Each adapter understands one named version; selection must use the original request’s version.
Connect version 1 and version 2 outputs to their matching ports. An unsupported version should not choose either branch.

investigation.title: A newer caller reaches yesterday’s parser
investigation.question: The changed request declares version 2 and sends query/count. What should change in the construction?
investigation.outcome: Retest the legacy default after repairing version 2 dispatch.

options.label: Select the version 2 adapter while retaining version 1
options.feedback: The server promised both versions. Replacing the old parser would break the other supported caller.

options.label: Ignore the version and prefer any available text field
options.feedback: That could silently choose an unintended operation in a mixed message.

connections.why: Each supported public version needs its own presence and value checks.
A renamed count must still request the same retrieval operation.

reflection.prompt: Which old client would fail if the server rolled back to version 1-only code?
reflection.carryForward: Keep supported public contracts distinct from the internal representation.

software-semantic-contracts.premise: The same pump looked different because its replacement sensor changed units.

construction.title: Keep fitted state in its training representation
construction.start: Build conversion from a scale and offset, then connect the stored centre and coefficient after it.
construction.outcome: The physical temperature, rather than the raw transport number, determines the score.
hints: Follow one reading through conversion before introducing the fitted centre.
The centre is already in Celsius. Subtract it after the scale-and-offset branch, then multiply by the coefficient.

investigation.title: The sensor changes units without changing temperature
investigation.question: The changed inputs are 68 F and 86 F. Predict the two scores after the saved Celsius preprocessing.
investigation.outcome: Compare both device representations; changing unit convention must not change these two predictions.
investigation.predictionLabel: Two illustrative scores in input order, as a JSON list

connections.skill: Keep the saved training centre fixed
connections.why: A fixed reference is still wrong if a request reaches it in another unit.
The named temperature now also needs a declared unit.

reflection.prompt: What would a Celsius-to-Fahrenheit change do if the model subtracted its centre before conversion?
reflection.carryForward: Save canonical units and preprocessing order with the fitted artifact.

preparation.title: Convert one representation before centring
preparation.challenge: Connect readings and the declared unit to both conversion components. Return Celsius values before applying fitted state.
preparation.why: The intermediate Celsius readings make an incorrect offset visible.
hints: Fahrenheit needs an offset as well as scaling.
A Celsius request should pass through unchanged.

software-tool-errors.premise: Repeating every failed call worked for a read, then risked creating a second job.

construction.title: Classify failure before deciding to repeat
construction.start: Place the outcome classifier before the recovery decision. Connect the repeat flags and budget as separate policy inputs.
construction.outcome: An unknown write outcome is investigated instead of retried blindly.
hints: A status category answers what was observed. The repeat flag answers a different question about the operation’s effect.
Unknown outcomes go to reconciliation first. Only a known transient category with repeat permission and remaining attempts reaches retry.

investigation.title: The transport loses a write response
investigation.question: One changed outcome is outcome_unknown. Which next step protects the existing operation identity?
investigation.outcome: Retest the known repeatable read and the exhausted budget after changing recovery.

options.label: Reconcile before attempting another create
options.feedback: The service may already have performed the write. A stable operation ID gives us something to check.

options.label: Retry because the network failed
options.feedback: A network failure tells us the caller lacks a response, not that the write failed.

connections.why: Clients also depend on stable error categories.
Retries must not silently create a different training run.

reflection.prompt: Which service guarantee would make an uncertain create safely repeatable?
reflection.carryForward: Record the operation identity and recovery outcome without inventing success.

software-contract-tests.premise: The original batch let a wrong request-local mean imitate the stored training reference.

construction.title: Make the fitted-state promise observable
construction.start: Build the transformation and an independent first-reading comparison. Keep the saved centre on the input side of both branches.
construction.outcome: A new neighbour cannot silently redefine the first pump’s transformed value.
hints: Build the numerical result before the check so Botie can inspect an actual discrepancy.
Read the first entry from that same result and compare it with the independently supplied expectation, using the declared tolerance.

investigation.title: The first reading stays 2 while its neighbour becomes 100
investigation.question: Should the first transformed reading change in this fitted row-wise contract?
investigation.outcome: Retest both baseline batches after repairing the reference branch.

options.label: No; its saved reference is still 4
options.feedback: The same pump retains the same input and fitted reference. Relearning a mean from this request would violate the contract.

options.label: Yes; use the new request mean
options.feedback: That would make the prediction depend on unrelated requests and would conceal the fitted-state bug.

connections.why: The earlier implementation rule now becomes an executable property.
The Python challenge checks a different invariance: aligned field permutation.

reflection.prompt: Could a constant transformation pass one relationship check while still failing the expected-value fixture?
reflection.carryForward: Use properties to discover counterexamples, then keep those incidents beside independent fixtures.

preparation.title: Inspect the actual transformed list
preparation.challenge: Return the batch after subtracting the stored centre, before adding a Boolean check.
preparation.why: A passing flag is easier to assess when the values it summarises remain visible.
hints: The stored centre is a source. A Mean tool applied to the current batch would learn a different reference.

data-partition-statistics.premise: A storage change should not reweight the training population.

construction.title: Combine the worker reports
construction.start: Keep sum and count on separate branches until their final division.
construction.outcome: The merged mean agrees with reading all records together.
hints: A small partition and a large partition do not deserve equal weight merely because each produced one mean.
Add the partition sums together and the partition counts together, then divide those totals. An empty partition contributes no observations.

investigation.title: One worker receives only a single hot reading
investigation.question: Predict the result for sums [30,90] and counts [3,1].
investigation.outcome: Compare with averaging 10 and 90; that would give the small file too much influence.

connections.skill: Build a mean from sum and count
connections.why: The same quantities now cross worker boundaries rather than one local list.

reflection.prompt: Which identifier prevents a retried partition from being added twice?
reflection.carryForward: A merge needs both mathematical validity and unique input contributions.

data-asof-features.premise: A correction from tomorrow makes yesterday’s training example look better than it could have been.

construction.title: Reconstruct the eligible records
construction.start: Keep event and availability comparisons separate until you combine their masks.
construction.outcome: Only values known at the decision reach the selection stage.
hints: A reading can occur before the decision and still arrive too late. Check both timestamps against the cutoff.
Combine the two inclusive checks record by record, then select the aligned values. Keep the original record order; this step filters eligible readings rather than choosing the latest one.

investigation.title: A newer event arrived after the decision
investigation.question: Should value 30 displace value 20 at time 10?
investigation.outcome: Inspect the remaining values before choosing the latest event.

options.label: No; it was only available at 12
options.feedback: The model running at 10 could not consume a later correction.

options.label: Yes; its event is newer
options.feedback: Event order alone ignores when the version reached the service.

connections.why: The two-clock eligibility rule now feeds historical feature retrieval.

reflection.prompt: What history would you need to reproduce a corrected feature next month?
reflection.carryForward: Preserve feature versions and their actual availability times.

data-contract-quarantine.premise: Botie’s cleaning step removes the night shift without raising a failure.

construction.title: Report what cleaning removed
construction.start: Build the range mask, use it to select values, and count its rejected complement.
construction.outcome: A small accepted file can no longer conceal a large rejection.
hints: Keep a flag beside each reading. Both endpoints belong to the accepted interval.
Use that flag to select accepted readings in their original order. Count the rejected flags separately so a discarded record does not disappear from the report.

investigation.title: The firmware batch arrives
investigation.question: For [20,-3,120], predict both the accepted list and rejected count.
investigation.outcome: Use the count to decide whether the producer needs investigation.

connections.why: The count now describes discarded observations as well as retained ones.

reflection.prompt: Which group-level report would reveal the missing night shift?
reflection.carryForward: A training release must inspect what preparation excluded.

data-stream-windows.premise: A delayed sensor backlog should not become evidence of the present condition.

construction.title: Build the event-time boundary
construction.start: Keep the lower comparison inclusive and the upper comparison strict before selecting readings.
construction.outcome: Every boundary event has exactly one adjacent window.
hints: The lower boundary belongs to this window; the upper boundary belongs to the next one. Using the same inclusive gate at both ends would count a boundary event twice.
Combine the lower and upper timestamp checks before selecting the aligned readings. Input arrival order need not be timestamp order.

investigation.title: An event lands exactly on the upper boundary
investigation.question: Should value 100 at event 20 enter the [10,20) result?
investigation.outcome: Run the old-backlog case and inspect which event survives.

options.label: No; it belongs to the next window
options.feedback: Excluding the upper bound prevents overlap between adjacent windows.

options.label: Yes; all threshold gates are inclusive
options.feedback: This boundary needs a strict comparison rather than the same gate at both ends.

connections.why: Window membership uses event time while feature availability still follows arrival and revision.

reflection.prompt: Which version would a decision made before the late packet use?
reflection.carryForward: Version emitted features and retain their availability timestamps.

data-artifact-lineage.premise: The jobs ran in the right order but reused features from an older dataset.

construction.title: Check the cache’s dependencies
construction.start: Compare the input and code identities on separate branches, then require both checks.
construction.outcome: A successful prior run is reusable only for compatible dependencies.
hints: An artifact depends on the input version and the transformation version. Keeping its filename does not keep those dependencies unchanged.
Compare both requested identities with their stored identities, then require both matches. A mismatch on either branch prevents reuse.

investigation.title: The file was replaced in place
investigation.question: The code is unchanged but the input version is d2. Should the d1 artifact be reused?
investigation.outcome: Change only the code next and verify the same invalidation rule.

options.label: No; input identity changed
options.feedback: The previous calculation belongs to a different dataset.

options.label: Yes; the job name stayed the same
options.feedback: A job name identifies a procedure, not every input version it has processed.

connections.skill: Keep outputs attached to a run
connections.why: Readiness now carries an explicit identity for the artifact it releases.

reflection.prompt: Which configuration setting could change a feature without changing the code?
reflection.carryForward: Include behaviour-changing configuration in artifact identity.

databricks-lazy-dataframes.premise: The sensor rule was written down, but the interface kept displaying the original records.

construction.title: Make the plan produce the requested table
construction.start: Construct the filter and projection before connecting the execution boundary to the current records.
construction.outcome: The result contains accepted records only, with their requested named fields.
hints: Start with the field comparison; projection comes afterwards so the checked field is still present.
Execute the plan needs both the completed plan and the current batch. Inspect its input record preview.

investigation.title: The next file still shows yesterday’s answer
investigation.question: The new file contains temperatures -1, 0 and 14, with a minimum of zero. What should we investigate first?
investigation.outcome: Trace the record wire, then predict which current records survive.

options.label: Whether the current batch reaches the execution component
options.feedback: A valid plan must be executed on the current records; a copied answer does not process a new batch.

options.label: Whether negative readings should be replaced with yesterday’s mean
options.feedback: Replacement is a different policy from the filter this lesson declared.

connections.skill: Keep record meaning while changing how work is organised
connections.why: Distributed execution still has to preserve which observations contributed.

reflection.prompt: Which operation in your construction actually needs the source rows?
reflection.carryForward: Keep source identity, transformation plan and materialised result distinct.

preparation.title: Write the plan before running it
preparation.challenge: Return a plan containing the declared filter and projection, without reading the current records.
preparation.why: Its output should describe instructions, not contain accepted sensor rows.

databricks-shuffle-skew.premise: The earlier filter accepts the correct records, but the grouped job waits for one busy pump.

construction.title: Expose and repair the hot route
construction.start: Create partial routing keys, then connect routing and worker counts. Inspect the records inside each worker.
construction.outcome: The same records reach workers through multiple partial groups without changing their original pump field.
hints: Keep pump untouched and add routingKey alongside it.
Route by the temporary key, then count every worker list, including empty ones.

investigation.title: A second route is opened for A
investigation.question: Four A records and one B are routed to two workers by the declared hash. Predict loads when A uses two salt groups.
investigation.outcome: Compare the load vector with the unsplit case, then check that its total still counts every record.

connections.why: The original pump identity must survive a routing-only transformation.

connections.skill: Merge the quantities that really add
connections.why: Partial groups require a correct final merge, not an unweighted average.

reflection.prompt: What evidence would justify salting a real Spark job rather than trusting this count-only picture?
reflection.carryForward: Keep logical group identity separate from temporary execution keys.

preparation.title: Prepare routing keys without losing pump identity
preparation.challenge: Return the records with their temporary routing keys, preserving every original record.
preparation.why: Inspect the hot records before a worker boundary hides why they were grouped.

databricks-delta-snapshots.premise: The routing repair still works, but a rerun silently reads a corrected table and changes the training evidence.

construction.title: Pin the input before calculating
construction.start: Choose the committed snapshot named by the run, then connect its field values to the existing mean calculation.
construction.outcome: A later table commit does not silently replace this run’s declared evidence.
hints: Open the requested version before extracting the field.
The input to Mean should be a column from one snapshot, not a list of all historical rows.

investigation.title: The code is identical but the mean changes
investigation.question: Version 0 has temperatures 10 and 20. Version 1 has 30 and 20. The model report names version 0, but its loader requests latest. What is the first repair?
investigation.outcome: Inspect the selected snapshot before changing the numerical procedure.

options.label: Make the loader request version 0 explicitly
options.feedback: The input must agree with the version recorded in the report.

options.label: Change the mean formula until the result is 15
options.feedback: The arithmetic is not the source of the mismatch.

connections.skill: Name the data that reaches the action
connections.why: A plan still needs a precise source identity.

connections.skill: Keep the inputs attached to their artifact
connections.why: The table version is part of the model’s evidence.

reflection.prompt: What else would need preserving before this old version could be called reproducible a year later?
reflection.carryForward: A version reference needs retained data, recorded dependencies and an explicit failure when unavailable.

preparation.title: Select the committed records
preparation.challenge: Return only the snapshot named by the run, before extracting a feature.
preparation.why: The table preview should show which records the numerical calculation will consume.

databricks-replay-safe-ingest.premise: A stable snapshot exposed a duplicate: the same input file contributed twice after a restart.

construction.title: Keep the retry from changing the dataset
construction.start: Select files absent from committed progress before connecting the atomic-state commit.
construction.outcome: The same discovery can be repeated without appending its records again.
hints: Compare file identities with the checkpoint, not row counts with the previous output.
The accepted-file list feeds the commit alongside the earlier rows and earlier checkpoint.

investigation.title: The acknowledgement disappears after success
investigation.question: The output already contains r1 and the checkpoint contains f1. The scheduler discovers f1 again. Predict the complete next state.
investigation.outcome: Progress and output must remain consistent even when the request is repeated.

connections.skill: Give a completed table state a durable identity
connections.why: A retry must preserve the intended logical state instead of appending another copy.

reflection.prompt: What would change if a producer overwrote a file under the same path?
reflection.carryForward: Treat source identity and checkpoint identity as part of the query contract.

preparation.title: Choose only uncommitted files
preparation.challenge: Return accepted file records before flattening or changing progress.
preparation.why: An empty accepted-file list on replay should be visible before the commit.

databricks-change-data-capture.premise: File replay is fixed, but different files contain out-of-order changes for the same pump.

construction.title: Preserve deletion evidence through the merge
construction.start: Select source versions before the merge, then separate stored state from its visible active view.
construction.outcome: A delayed older change cannot recreate an entity deleted by a newer source version.
hints: Use seq for ordering and pump for identity; delivery position has no authority here.
Keep deleted rows through the merge. Hide them only on the final consumer branch.

investigation.title: The pump reappears after deletion
investigation.question: Stored state says P7 was deleted at sequence 9. The next file carries an active P7 at sequence 8. What has the broken machine forgotten?
investigation.outcome: Inspect retained state rather than only the active-row output.

options.label: The deletion’s source sequence
options.feedback: That version is needed to recognise the arriving record as older.

options.label: The order in which the file names sort
options.feedback: File-name order does not define the entity’s authoritative source sequence.

connections.skill: Separate a repeated file from a new file
connections.why: A genuinely new file can still carry an old entity version.

reflection.prompt: Which source guarantee would allow your system to retire an old tombstone safely?
reflection.carryForward: Retain ordering evidence for as long as older messages can arrive.

preparation.title: Find an unambiguous last change per pump
preparation.challenge: Return the highest source-sequence change for each entity before touching target state.
preparation.why: The source stage must resolve multiplicity before a target row can be updated.

databricks-lakeflow-quality.premise: The versioned merge is correct, but a warning was mistaken for a gate and invalid values reached training.

construction.title: Make the chosen policy control publication
construction.start: Evaluate rows first, then connect their flags to the publication policy and earlier dataset.
construction.outcome: The output rows and status now agree with the declared consequence of failure.
hints: Do not drop rows while evaluating the predicate; the policy may require keeping or rejecting the entire candidate.
The publication component needs the earlier snapshot as well as the new checked rows.

investigation.title: The failure count is nonzero but every row remains
investigation.question: The pipeline retained 10,-1,20 under a declared warning policy. What is wrong with expecting the invalid row to disappear?
investigation.outcome: Choose a policy from the training contract, then predict its effect before running.

options.label: A warning does not declare a drop or failure policy
options.feedback: The check can be working exactly as configured while the chosen policy is inappropriate.

options.label: Every expectation silently clips negative values to zero
options.feedback: Clipping is not one of the stated publication policies.

connections.why: A platform quality policy must implement the intended rejection boundary.

connections.skill: Distinguish an older published snapshot from a failed candidate
connections.why: Failure must not make stale data appear newly produced.

reflection.prompt: What evidence should an operator see when a failed update leaves the previous dataset in service?
reflection.carryForward: Retain the candidate failure reason and the identity/age of the dataset that remains published.

preparation.title: Attach the quality evidence to each row
preparation.challenge: Return complete records with pass flags before choosing any publication consequence.
preparation.why: A count should remain traceable to the records that produced it.

databricks-mlflow-lineage.premise: Quality checks pass, but the new winning model was measured against different validation evidence.

construction.title: Keep the score attached to the comparison and artifact
construction.start: Build an eligible-run shortlist before choosing minimum MAE, then preserve the chosen run’s manifest.
construction.outcome: The selected artifact belongs to a run assessed on the declared validation evidence.
hints: Start with the validation table identity, its version, split and role. Looking only at version numbers can mix unrelated histories.
Return the chosen model URI together with both table identities, their versions and the assessment split. Different training tables can be the intended experiment.

investigation.title: A perfect test score enters the shortlist
investigation.question: Both records use lab.validation.sensor_readings version 4 and split S. One has role=test and MAE zero; the other has role=validation and MAE three. Which issue must the selector repair?
investigation.outcome: Check role, validation table identity, its version and split before comparing MAE.

options.label: The assessment-role filter
options.feedback: A final-test result must not be used to choose the validation winner.

options.label: The precision of the number zero
options.feedback: The score’s role determines whether it belongs in this selection.

connections.skill: Know which dataset was actually published
connections.why: A run must refer to the data it measured, including whether an older snapshot remained in use.

connections.skill: Keep model selection separate from final assessment
connections.why: The comparison cannot recruit a final-test score as another validation candidate.

reflection.prompt: Would a deterministic tie-break justify saying one model is better?
reflection.carryForward: Preserve the evidence and uncertainty behind a choice, not only the selected model label.

preparation.title: Identify genuinely comparable validation runs
preparation.challenge: Return only validation-role runs using the declared validation table identity, version and split.
preparation.why: Inspecting the shortlist before sorting lets us see which tempting scores answer a different question.

databricks-unity-catalog-access.premise: The run manifest names a valid table, but the scheduled training identity cannot read it.

construction.title: Trace permission through the complete table name
construction.start: List the catalog, schema and table requirements before comparing explicit grants for this job.
construction.outcome: The refusal identifies a missing boundary without returning protected records.
hints: SELECT on a table does not supply its enclosing usage requirements in this model.
Each requirement needs a grant for this principal or an already established group, not just any grant on the object.

investigation.title: A colleague’s grant appears in the evidence
investigation.question: All three privileges belong to job-A; the current principal is job-B. Why must the construction refuse?
investigation.outcome: Keep principal, privilege and object attached while checking each boundary.

options.label: The privileges belong to a different identity
options.feedback: Matching object names do not transfer another principal’s authority.

options.label: The table must be corrupt
options.feedback: The shown evidence establishes an identity mismatch, not damaged data.

connections.why: A manifest identifies what to read; it does not authorise the job to read it.

connections.skill: Keep query values separate from database authority
connections.why: Accepting a value in a query never grants the caller permission to read its source.

reflection.prompt: Where must this permission be enforced after a browser workshop says allow?
reflection.carryForward: The authoritative data service must check the executing identity and current policy.

preparation.title: Resolve the object boundaries
preparation.challenge: Return the three explicit read requirements implied by the complete table name.
preparation.why: Inspecting each object prevents a short table name from hiding another namespace.

databricks-historical-features.premise: Access is correct, but the latest-value join gives past predictions information published later.

construction.title: Build the feature candidates for each decision
construction.start: Keep each prediction’s entity and time beside its candidates, then select the newest eligible published value.
construction.outcome: Future, stale and wrong-entity values cannot silently fill a historical model input.
hints: Match the entity first and exclude later publication times before selecting a maximum.
A latest explicit null is not permission to search backward for a nonnull value.

investigation.title: The newest value was published after the prediction
investigation.question: P7 at minute 6 sees values published at 3 and 8. A broken join chooses the minute-8 correction because its event was earlier. What should be repaired?
investigation.outcome: Predict the eligible candidate list before choosing its newest row.

options.label: The availability boundary before latest-value selection
options.feedback: A correction’s old event label does not make its newly published value available earlier.

options.label: The prediction’s timestamp should move forward until the result looks good
options.feedback: Changing the decision time rewrites the prediction problem.

connections.skill: Respect what was available at the decision
connections.why: The platform lookup must preserve that same historical boundary.
A timestamp filter cannot recover overwritten historical contents.

reflection.prompt: What evidence shows that publishedAt really records availability rather than a backdated event?
reflection.carryForward: Keep publication history, table identity and the lookup/fallback policy with the trained procedure.

preparation.title: Keep eligible candidates beside each prediction
preparation.challenge: Return one candidate group per prediction after entity, time and age filtering.
preparation.why: An empty candidate group should remain visible rather than being replaced by another pump’s recent value.

systems-inference-batching.premise: Botie’s batch throughput improves while the earliest user waits longer.

construction.title: Put waiting back into the latency report
construction.start: Connect dispatch and execution to a common completion, then subtract the arrival vector.
construction.outcome: The report follows each user rather than dividing a shared duration.
hints: Requests share a completion time but have different arrival times. The earliest request also pays for waiting while the batch fills.
Combine dispatch time and execution duration first. Subtract each request’s arrival from that common completion; dividing execution time by batch size would measure something else.

investigation.title: The third image delays dispatch
investigation.question: Predict the three latencies when the batch waits until time 6.
investigation.outcome: Inspect the first request before deciding whether the larger batch helps the service objective.

connections.why: Queueing time now belongs to individual requests in a shared inference batch.

reflection.prompt: Which traffic pattern would make a full-batch-only policy unusable?
reflection.carryForward: Benchmark the arrival process as well as the model invocation.

systems-agent-deadlines.premise: Every service used a reasonable timeout, but the sequence exceeded its overall deadline.

construction.title: Carry the budget through the run
construction.start: Subtract elapsed work and reserve before connecting the allowance to the next step.
construction.outcome: Later calls cannot spend time that earlier calls already consumed.
hints: The next tool must fit inside what remains of the whole run. It cannot begin again with the original timeout.
Remove elapsed time and the response reserve before setting a new-call allowance. If that leaves less than zero, return zero rather than a negative timeout.

investigation.title: The response reserve has already started
investigation.question: After 950 ms of a 1000 ms budget with a 100 ms reserve, may another ordinary tool call start?
investigation.outcome: Try a larger overall budget without changing elapsed time.

options.label: No; its available allowance is zero
options.feedback: The remaining total time is already smaller than the reserved response time.

options.label: Yes; give it the original second
options.feedback: That resets the whole budget and recreates the overrun.

connections.why: The end-to-end clock now constrains a sequence of agent operations.

reflection.prompt: What would a timeout after a successful write leave uncertain?
reflection.carryForward: Track effect identity and reconcile uncertain outcomes separately from timing.

systems-kv-cache-memory.premise: The parameter budget passed, then a long conversation exhausted the remaining memory.

construction.title: Account for cached tokens
construction.start: Add the retained sequence lengths, then connect the storage needed per token.
construction.outcome: The estimate grows when conversations grow, even with fixed weights.
hints: The cache keeps per-token state for every active sequence. A completed sequence with no retained tokens contributes no token storage to this estimate.
Total the current retained lengths before applying the supplied bytes per token. This counts dense logical storage; allocator blocks and other runtime allocations are outside this small estimate.

investigation.title: The second conversation reaches fifty tokens
investigation.question: Predict the new byte count before admitting another request.
investigation.outcome: Check how much one long sequence contributes to the sum.

connections.why: Cached attention state is another allocation whose lifetime differs from model weights.

reflection.prompt: How much future generation would an admission policy reserve?
reflection.carryForward: Measure peak allocation and enforce a declared generation bound.

systems-context-cache.premise: An answer cached for one team reaches another because the wording matched.

construction.title: Include the context in reuse
construction.start: Compare the question and context records on independent branches, then require both.
construction.outcome: A matching question cannot override a context mismatch.
hints: The same question can have a different answer for another team or another manual version. Keep the question and its context as separate dependencies.
Compare the whole supplied context record as well as the question, then require both matches. These equality checks assume permissions and expiry have already been checked elsewhere.

investigation.title: Another team asks the same question
investigation.question: Should the team-A cached response be reused for team B?
investigation.outcome: Change the manual version and inspect the same boundary again.

options.label: No; its authority context differs
options.feedback: Shared wording does not establish permission to use the same evidence.

options.label: Yes; the question is identical
options.feedback: The answer’s dependencies extend beyond its text.

connections.skill: Name the inputs that produced an artifact
connections.why: A cached response is another artifact whose dependencies must be explicit.

reflection.prompt: What should a permission revocation do to already cached answers?
reflection.carryForward: Recheck current authority and expire or invalidate affected entries.

serving-prefill-decode.premise: Botie starts two equally long answers at different times. A shared throughput number does not tell the technician which wait changed.

construction.title: Put two kinds of waiting on separate branches
construction.start: Take the first emission minus arrival, then keep the neighbouring token gaps beside it.
construction.outcome: The output distinguishes an empty screen from an interrupted stream.
hints: The first emitted timestamp belongs on the arrival subtraction branch.
Later pauses need adjacent differences, not division by the number of output tokens.

investigation.title: The first token stays put, but the last one stalls
investigation.question: Arrival is 0 ms and emissions are [140,170,230] ms. Predict [first-token wait, list of later gaps], then compare the two branches with the evenly spaced case.
investigation.outcome: A later pause can worsen while time to first token remains unchanged.

connections.skill: Measure each request from its own arrival
connections.why: A generated answer adds several completion boundaries inside one request.

reflection.prompt: Which timestamp would distinguish queue waiting from prompt processing?
reflection.carryForward: Keep measurement boundaries with any latency number you compare.

serving-prefix-reuse.premise: Botie already accounts for KV memory. Now repeated manual prefixes offer a way to avoid some prompt work, provided the state is compatible.

construction.title: Connect a leading-token match to a compatibility gate
construction.start: Build the reusable-token count, then require agreement on the stated model and namespace contract.
construction.outcome: A plausible token match alone cannot authorise reuse.
hints: First ask whether the stored arrays belong to the same configuration and namespace.
The prefix counter stops at the first differing ID. Round its result down, then make a failed compatibility decision produce zero.

investigation.title: Identical tokens arrive under a new adapter
investigation.question: The cached and incoming token lists match, but the adapter field differs. Which earlier assumption fails?
investigation.outcome: The correct repair keeps a compatibility branch beside the prefix counter.

options.label: The saved keys and values were calculated under the same model configuration
options.feedback: The adapter can change those arrays, so this contract rejects reuse.

options.label: Equal token IDs guarantee equal attention state
options.feedback: The IDs identify inputs; the model configuration also affects their calculated state.

connections.why: Reuse changes how some state is computed or shared; it does not make storage free.
The saved work belongs primarily to repeated prompt processing, not a complete cached answer.

reflection.prompt: What else would need versioning if the request included an image encoder output?
reflection.carryForward: Treat reusable computation as versioned state with explicit boundaries.

serving-continuous-admission.premise: The earlier batch timing still describes waiting, but generated responses finish at different iteration boundaries. Botie needs a group that can change.

construction.title: Rebuild the next group from remaining work
construction.start: Remove finished sequences and build separate free-slot and free-block branches before admitting waiting IDs.
construction.outcome: A sequence joins only when both its place and its storage fit.
hints: Keep only rows with remaining output tokens before measuring occupied capacity.
Add each waiting prompt and output allowance, round up to blocks, then consume slots and blocks in FIFO order.

investigation.title: The same free slot faces a longer prompt
investigation.question: C now needs five blocks while only four are free. Why does the earlier slot-only construction fail?
investigation.outcome: Repair the admission path without evicting an unfinished sequence or silently changing FIFO.

options.label: It never checked the memory reservation
options.feedback: One place in a batch does not guarantee enough KV blocks.

options.label: Finished A still needs all its output iterations
options.feedback: A has zero remaining tokens in the stated fixture and releases its reservation.

connections.why: Admission must account for the new sequence’s storage, not only model weights.
A reservation rounds upward to whole blocks, unlike reusable prefix length.

reflection.prompt: When might skipping an unfit head help utilisation, and whose waiting time could worsen?
reflection.carryForward: State the scheduling policy beside its capacity calculation.

serving-cancellation-pressure.premise: The earlier scheduler released finished sequences. A cancellation request looks finished to the reader before the worker confirms it has released anything.

construction.title: Add an acknowledgement boundary before freeing capacity
construction.start: Apply worker release acknowledgements and keep every other owned row in the capacity report. Bound the waiting queue separately.
construction.outcome: Clicking Stop does not create a fictitious free slot.
hints: The acknowledgement list identifies which cancellation requests actually released resources.
After applying those events, count held rows and sum their blocks. The waiting queue has its own limit and rejected-arrival list.

investigation.title: The display stopped but no release arrived
investigation.question: A is cancellation-requested with no acknowledgement. Which repair belongs between the user event and the capacity counter?
investigation.outcome: Compare the same rows after A’s acknowledgement, without changing waiting arrivals.

options.label: Wait for the engine’s release evidence
options.feedback: A remains owned until the execution layer confirms its release.

options.label: Treat every user cancellation as immediate free memory
options.feedback: The worker may still need the reservation while stopping.

connections.skill: Count resources before admitting another sequence
connections.why: A release now needs an authoritative lifecycle event, not only an abandoned display.
Waiting or retrying must not create a new full deadline for an old request.

reflection.prompt: Which record would tell you whether an earlier booking tool had already committed?
reflection.carryForward: Track resource release separately from external effect reconciliation.

serving-canary-effects.premise: Botie can route traffic to a candidate, but a duplicated maintenance question can duplicate its booking unless the effect path has a separate boundary.

construction.title: Keep model choice out of the write-authority rule
construction.start: Build one branch for routing and another for capability plus non-shadow status, then attach both to each run ID.
construction.outcome: A model experiment does not silently become a second live actor.
hints: Route from buckets and percentage without using those values as permissions.
For write authority, require capability and a zero shadow flag. Preserve each result beside its own run ID.

investigation.title: The comparison run inherits a broad capability
investigation.question: The copied run has capability1 and shadow1. What must prevent the second booking?
investigation.outcome: Check an unauthorised stable-model request too; model version must never substitute for permission.

options.label: An enforced non-shadow requirement at the effect boundary
options.feedback: The shadow status must deny live writes independently of the selected model.

options.label: Hiding the candidate’s response from the screen
options.feedback: The booking tool can act before any text reaches the screen.

connections.why: Hiding, cancelling or rerouting an answer cannot undo an action already committed.
A comparison run must not manufacture another live write under a fresh effect key.

reflection.prompt: What evidence would establish that the real booking service rejects shadow credentials?
reflection.carryForward: Enforce effect authority where an action can occur, not in generated prose.

robot-perception-frames.premise: The detector’s coordinates were correct for the camera but wrong for Botie’s planner.

construction.title: Connect the coordinate frames
construction.start: Rotate the point first, then add the destination-frame offset.
construction.outcome: The same observed point can be expressed in the planner’s frame.
hints: Camera coordinates describe directions from the camera. First express that direction using the robot’s axes.
Apply the rotation to the point before adding the camera origin expressed in the robot frame. Rotating the translation too would describe a different transformation.

investigation.title: The camera rotates on its mount
investigation.question: Should simply adding [1,3] still produce the correct robot point?
investigation.outcome: Check the backwards-facing case for sign errors.

options.label: No; the point’s directions changed too
options.feedback: The rotation must act on camera coordinates before adding the robot-frame offset.

options.label: Yes; only the origin matters
options.feedback: A sideways camera has different axes as well as a displaced origin.

connections.skill: Apply a matrix to a vector
connections.why: The matrix now has a physical meaning: expressing coordinates in a different frame.

reflection.prompt: What additional input is needed when the camera mount moves?
reflection.carryForward: Associate each measurement with its frame and capture time.

robot-observation-latency.premise: The coordinate adapter works, but the object moves while Botie waits for inference.

construction.title: Add a motion prediction after the frame adapter
construction.start: Use velocity and elapsed time to calculate displacement in the same frame as the position.
construction.outcome: A captured location becomes a time-qualified prediction.
hints: The detector reports where the object was when the image was captured. Velocity describes how that position changes while the result travels.
Find displacement from velocity and observation age, then add it to the captured position in the same frame. This assumes constant velocity over that interval.

investigation.title: The image is four tenths of a second old
investigation.question: Predict the position for velocity [0.5,0] before running the propagation.
investigation.outcome: Compare against the unchanged old coordinate to see the latency error.

connections.why: Position and velocity must agree on directions before a time update makes sense.

reflection.prompt: Which unobserved acceleration would invalidate this update?
reflection.carryForward: Carry age and uncertainty with a predicted position.

robot-feedback-corrections.premise: A single predicted move leaves an error that the next action must measure.

construction.title: Close the correction loop
construction.start: Calculate target minus position, scale the correction, and update the position.
construction.outcome: A new measured position changes the next command.
hints: The correction must point towards the target. A position beyond the target therefore needs an error with the opposite sign.
Find target minus measured position, scale by the gain and update interval, then add the movement to the current position. A large gain can carry the next position past the target.

investigation.title: The gain increases to 1.5
investigation.question: Will the next position stop short, land on target, or pass it? Predict the value.
investigation.outcome: The answer is 12, so the next correction must reverse direction.

connections.why: Feedback depends on a measurement whose frame and age are understood.

reflection.prompt: What happens when gain times timestep exceeds two in this plant?
reflection.carryForward: Evaluate the trajectory and peaks, not only one prediction.

robot-actuator-windup.premise: The proportional loop now needs memory, and that memory grows while the motor is unable to comply.

construction.title: Feed actuator limits back to memory
construction.start: Keep requested and clipped commands on separate branches, then use their difference in the integral update.
construction.outcome: The next stored contribution reflects the applied command.
hints: The requested command uses the old integral contribution. Keep it separate from the bounded command the actuator can actually apply.

Update the stored contribution using the ordinary error term and the applied-minus-requested mismatch, both over the supplied time interval. When the upper limit clips a request, that mismatch pulls back against further accumulation.

investigation.title: The request exceeds the actuator limit
investigation.question: Will clipping 11 to 3 alone prevent the integral state from growing?
investigation.outcome: Reverse the error and verify that the correction reverses too.

options.label: No; update the memory using the mismatch
options.feedback: The stored state otherwise continues to integrate the unreachable demand.

options.label: Yes; the output is already bounded
options.feedback: A bounded output can conceal an unbounded internal request.

connections.why: The earlier proportional branch now combines with state and a physical limit.

reflection.prompt: Which recovery trajectory would reveal excessive stored demand?
reflection.carryForward: Test the return from saturation and keep actuator limits in the loop.

state-predict-correct.premise: The earlier motion projection moves a point forward in time. A new noisy detection now disagrees with that projection, so Botie needs an uncertainty-weighted correction.

construction.title: Build the correction rather than always replacing the position
construction.start: Predict both quantities, calculate the innovation and gain, then assemble the corrected mean and variance.
construction.outcome: The observation influences the estimate according to its stated reliability.
hints: Predict uncertainty as well as motion. The old variance alone misses the new motion error.
Use the gain on measurement minus predicted mean. The variance branch keeps both weighted error contributions.

investigation.title: The same camera reading becomes less reliable
investigation.question: Keep prediction4 m and prior variance 4 m², but change camera variance to16 m². Predict the named mean and variance after correction.
investigation.outcome: The mean moves less toward the reading and the remaining variance is larger.

connections.skill: Combine independent evidence with stated variances
connections.why: The motion prediction now supplies one side of the same reliability calculation.

connections.skill: Predict a position at the observation time
connections.why: Measurement and prediction must describe the same time and frame before their difference is meaningful.

reflection.prompt: What would invalidate adding the two error variances?
reflection.carryForward: Carry the independence and model assumptions with the uncertainty numbers.

preparation.title: Correct the position before assembling the full record
preparation.challenge: Build the predicted mean, gain and innovation branch that returns the corrected position.
preparation.why: It shows which measurement difference is being weighted before adding the uncertainty branch.
hints: The innovation compares the camera with the predicted position at its timestamp.
The gain uses predicted variance, including the motion-error contribution.

state-missing-observations.premise: The earlier filter expected a number from every camera frame. An occlusion now removes one observation while the object continues moving.

construction.title: Give prediction and optional correction their own places
construction.start: Connect the first prediction and available correction before feeding their result into the next interval.
construction.outcome: A missing observation supplies no invented position and no invented information.
hints: None is a missing marker. Zero must still follow the ordinary numeric correction path.
Connect prediction, optional update, prediction, optional update in that order. Each interval adds its own supplied process variance.

investigation.title: The first frame disappears
investigation.question: Why would filling the missing first measurement with0 m produce another result?
investigation.outcome: The repair preserves the predicted state until actual observation data arrives.

options.label: It would assert a real observation at the origin
options.feedback: Zero would attract the estimated position and reduce variance under the observation model.

options.label: Skipping the correction stops the belt
options.feedback: Motion prediction still advances the state before the next measurement.

connections.skill: Keep prediction separate from measurement correction
connections.why: The correction can be omitted without discarding motion or uncertainty propagation.
Missing a frame and receiving an old frame late are different timing situations.

reflection.prompt: What must change if an observation arrives out of timestamp order?
reflection.carryForward: Represent unavailable evidence explicitly and keep the estimate’s time.

preparation.title: Carry the first boundary into the second
preparation.challenge: Build the second motion prediction from the result of the first optional update.
preparation.why: This makes the temporal dependency visible before the final camera correction.

state-gating-association.premise: The earlier filter accepted the supplied observation as belonging to its part. A crowded frame now contains several plausible observations, so that identity assumption must be checked.

construction.title: Put compatibility and ambiguity before the correction
construction.start: Build the scaled disagreement list and pass mask. Give the optional update a measurement only when one candidate remains.
construction.outcome: An unresolved match leaves the predicted state visible rather than generating false certainty.
hints: The denominator includes prediction uncertainty and measurement uncertainty.
Threshold gate returns1when its first input is at least its second: connect threshold first and the distance list second. Exactly one pass is needed.

investigation.title: Another part appears inside the gate
investigation.question: Both10.5 m and9.5 m pass around a10 m prediction. Why must the exact-one rule skip the update?
investigation.outcome: The missing-observation route is now useful for unresolved identity as well as an absent camera frame.

options.label: The numerical test has not resolved which object supplied the observation
options.feedback: Both observations are plausible, but this fixture supplies no further identity evidence.

options.label: The smallest variance must always be zero
options.feedback: Skipping an ambiguous observation preserves the prediction’s nonzero uncertainty.

connections.why: Ambiguous association can also produce no usable measurement for this track.

connections.skill: Choose a distance with the right meaning
connections.why: The covariance-scaled innovation replaces an unqualified raw position distance.

reflection.prompt: What extra evidence could distinguish two candidates without changing their positions?
reflection.carryForward: Keep compatibility, identity and correction as separate decisions.

preparation.title: Inspect which candidate survives before updating
preparation.challenge: Return the single numeric candidate or null after computing and applying the gate.
preparation.why: The association output reveals ambiguity before it is hidden in a corrected mean.

state-model-uncertainty.premise: The earlier filter still produces a clean mean and variance when its motion model misses an acceleration. Botie now needs to test what those numbers claim.

construction.title: Keep truth outside the estimation branch
construction.start: Reuse prediction and correction, then compare their final estimate with the separate simulated reference.
construction.outcome: A precise-looking result can visibly fail its own declared uncertainty scale.
hints: Finish estimation without using the reference source. The reference belongs on its own evaluation input.
Compare signed error and squared error relative to declared variance. A covered case can still be imprecise, and one case never proves calibration.

investigation.title: The camera repeatedly lies ahead of the prediction
investigation.question: The changed interval adds almost no motion uncertainty while actual displacement is larger than expected. What should be investigated?
investigation.outcome: The broader-variance case illustrates a consequence to evaluate, not an automatic tuning prescription.

options.label: The motion/error model and the signed innovation pattern
options.feedback: Understated process uncertainty makes this filter resist an informative measurement.

options.label: Whether truth can be wired directly into the prediction to improve the score
options.feedback: That would leak the evaluation answer into the estimator and invalidate the test.

connections.why: The covariance is now evaluated rather than accepted simply because the formula returned it.

connections.skill: Separate state estimation from action selection
connections.why: A controller needs a state estimate, but this diagnostic does not choose a safe action.

reflection.prompt: Which held-out motion conditions would distinguish a model repair from a wider error bar?
reflection.carryForward: Assess uncertainty width, actual error and their relationship on independent trajectories.

security-retrieval-authority.premise: The most relevant manual is private to another tenant.

construction.title: Place permission before evidence consumption
construction.start: Combine tenant membership and the resolved document grant before selecting IDs.
construction.outcome: Only authorised evidence can enter a later ranking or prompt.
hints: A relevant document can still belong to another customer. Relevance does not supply permission.
Require both the current tenant match and the application’s resolved document grant before selecting the corresponding IDs. The supplied grant flags stand in for checks made by a trusted service.

investigation.title: A high score crosses a customer boundary
investigation.question: May a strong match override a failed tenant check?
investigation.outcome: Try a same-tenant record whose document grant is revoked.

options.label: No; the service must exclude it
options.feedback: Relevance provides no authority to access another customer’s record.

options.label: Yes; it helps answer accurately
options.feedback: An accurate answer can still disclose information without permission.

connections.why: The candidate set must now be authorised before its final shortlist is formed.

reflection.prompt: Where else could a forbidden title leak after the body is filtered?
reflection.carryForward: Apply the data boundary to logs, caches and citations too.

security-private-aggregates.premise: A nameless report still lets one extreme contribution move the result substantially.

construction.title: Calculate influence before adding any noise
construction.start: Clip values on the mean branch and use the public range and count on the sensitivity branch.
construction.outcome: The influence bound remains visible separately from the statistic.
hints: Bound each person’s contribution before calculating the mean. Use the declared public bounds, not bounds fitted to the observed values.

The second output measures how much one replacement contribution could change that mean, using the public range and fixed participant count. The exact mean remains an exact release; this construction has not added a privacy mechanism.

investigation.title: One contribution jumps to one hundred
investigation.question: Predict both clipped mean and sensitivity for [2,4,100].
investigation.outcome: The observed extreme changes the clipped mean, while the sensitivity still follows the declared range.

connections.why: The denominator now participates in a precisely stated influence bound.

reflection.prompt: Why would one hundred rows from one person break this interpretation?
reflection.carryForward: State the protected unit and account for repeated releases.

security-model-artifacts.premise: A downloaded file is data to the transport but may be executable behaviour to its loader.

construction.title: Put verification before loading
construction.start: Combine trusted byte verification with loader-policy acceptance before selecting artifact IDs.
construction.outcome: The selected path requires both provenance evidence and an acceptable loading method.
hints: Matching approved bytes and using an approved loader answer different questions. Neither check can replace the other.
Require both flags for each artifact, then select its ID. The workshop consumes verifier results; it does not inspect a downloaded file or execute its loader.

investigation.title: A trusted digest meets an unsafe loader
investigation.question: May artifact C load merely because its digest matches?
investigation.outcome: Try the case where every digest matches but no loader is approved.

options.label: No; its loader policy still fails
options.feedback: Matching approved bytes does not by itself permit the chosen execution behaviour.

options.label: Yes; every matching file is safe
options.feedback: A digest proves equality with expected bytes, not harmlessness.

connections.why: We now distinguish identifying an artifact from trusting its origin and loading behaviour.

reflection.prompt: Which review becomes stale when the loader version changes?
reflection.carryForward: Bind release evidence to the artifact and its execution environment.

security-training-provenance.premise: A label-review-only filter worked until a new source entered through the same numerical interface.

construction.title: Build the training-release boundary before the fit
construction.start: Keep source and label evidence on separate branches, combine their masks, then filter IDs and targets together.
construction.outcome: An attractive training result cannot substitute for a record’s release evidence.
hints: Use the same combined mask for identities and targets.
Keep the empty accepted list visible as no evidence. Do not invent a zero baseline.

investigation.title: A new feed claims its labels are reviewed
investigation.question: The proposed row has reviewed=true but its resolved source is not approved. May its target enter this release?
investigation.outcome: Retest the unresolved label from the familiar source as well.

options.label: No; source approval is still missing
options.feedback: Completed review does not replace the independent source policy.

options.label: Yes; a numerical reviewed target is enough
options.feedback: That would let the new contribution channel bypass the boundary this release promised.

connections.skill: Trace fitted results to exact inputs
connections.why: The record identity must survive filtering and fitting.
Expected bytes and familiar names do not establish truthful training labels.

reflection.prompt: Which approved-source compromise would this gate fail to detect?
reflection.carryForward: Record what the filter establishes, and keep independent evaluation outside the same contribution channel.

preparation.title: Inspect eligibility before seeing its fitted effect
preparation.challenge: Build one flag per proposed record, requiring both source approval and completed review.
preparation.why: This separates the release decision from the numerical effect of fitting.
hints: Both pieces of evidence must describe the same row.
A reviewed proposal from an unapproved source still needs a zero flag.

security-backdoor-evaluation.premise: The clean metric looked reassuring because it never asked about the changed input condition.

construction.title: Build a report that can expose conditional failure
construction.start: Keep clean correctness on one branch. On another, define the eligible pair set before counting target hits.
construction.outcome: A high clean score remains visible without excusing a measured failure on the declared condition.
hints: Keep clean accuracy and the conditional test on separate branches.
Count target hits only where the eligibility flag is 1, and show the count beside its denominator.

investigation.title: Clean predictions stay fixed while changed predictions become safe
investigation.question: Which evidence must change in the report?
investigation.outcome: Retest the all-target population so an empty denominator remains unavailable rather than zero.

options.label: The targeted-success count, not the unchanged clean accuracy
options.feedback: The observations differ only on changed inputs, so the two metrics must remain separate.

options.label: Only clean accuracy; one score is enough
options.feedback: The ordinary predictions did not change and cannot describe the newly tested condition.

connections.skill: Keep evaluation outside the contribution channel
connections.why: A conditional failure needs its own reviewed evidence rather than a reassuring training story.

connections.skill: Name the population behind a metric
connections.why: The new denominator is a specifically eligible paired subset.

reflection.prompt: Which additional evidence would distinguish an implanted condition from an ordinary model weakness?
reflection.carryForward: Preserve paired case identities, denominators and ordinary task quality when reviewing a repair.

preparation.title: Choose the eligible paired examples
preparation.challenge: Mark clean-correct non-target examples only when the supplied edit has been reviewed as label-preserving.
preparation.why: The denominator must be established before a target-hit rate can be interpreted.
hints: A true target-class example is not a newly induced target prediction.
An already incorrect clean prediction does not enter this lesson’s induced-failure denominator.

security-adversarial-threat-models.premise: The initial small test passed, but a deliberately selected allowed change reached a different side of the boundary.

construction.title: Build the model and the scope checks side by side
construction.start: Start with the weighted-sum classifier. Keep the change-budget, domain and fixed-coordinate checks on a separate branch before combining the report.
construction.outcome: A wrong prediction is interpreted under the exact capability we declared.
hints: First construct the two predictions from the actual vectors and fixed weights.
Keep the scope branch independent. A null observed_failure can mean the comparison is excluded, so inspect its diagnostic fields.

investigation.title: The allowed first coordinate reaches 0.5
investigation.question: Both inputs sum to the cutoff. Is this a relevant new failure under the stated fixture label?
investigation.outcome: Retest the larger out-of-budget change without counting it as an in-scope failure.

options.label: Yes; it is in scope and the original was correct
options.feedback: The supplied change respects the budget and fixed-coordinate rule while the model’s inclusive cutoff now predicts 1.

options.label: No; the clean test had passed
options.feedback: The clean result says nothing about this additional allowed input.

connections.skill: Follow a weighted sum into a decision
connections.why: The familiar threshold now gives a visible decision boundary.
The capability checks define which prediction changes answer this experiment’s question.

reflection.prompt: Which claim would remain untested even after every supplied case passes?
reflection.carryForward: Record the capability, label assumptions and search coverage beside each robustness result.

preparation.title: Decide whether the supplied trial is in scope
preparation.challenge: Combine the size limit, fixed-coordinate rule and public domain checks into one flag of 0 or 1.
preparation.why: We must know what capability a trial represents before interpreting its failure.
hints: A permitted size does not allow a change to a protected coordinate.
The epsilon value goes before the measured largest change in a Threshold gate.

security-prediction-api-controls.premise: A request-count limit looked effective until batching changed the work inside one message.

construction.title: Reserve the actual prediction work
construction.start: Build a caller-row branch and a global-unit branch, then require both before projecting the public response.
construction.outcome: A batch cannot obtain a prediction merely because it fits one of the two independent allowances.
hints: Subtract prior use separately from each allowance.
Require both capacity flags, then pass the result into the public-label component. A denied request should not expose its internal score.

investigation.title: One envelope now carries 6 rows
investigation.question: The caller has 5 rows left. Does the single envelope fit this policy?
investigation.outcome: Retest the independently exhausted global budget before returning any public label.

options.label: No; the work exceeds the remaining row allowance
options.feedback: This quota is expressed in evaluated rows, so the request envelope cannot reset its meaning.

options.label: Yes; the HTTP request count increased only once
options.feedback: That is the assumption the larger batch exposes.

connections.why: A caller’s identity and resource state cannot come from a model’s untrusted claim.

connections.skill: Keep retries inside an operation budget
connections.why: Repeated calls and batches participate in the same resource accounting.

reflection.prompt: Which information does a label-only interface still reveal to repeated callers?
reflection.carryForward: Keep access, admitted work and public response detail as explicit service policies.

preparation.title: Construct admission before exposing output
preparation.challenge: Require the batch to fit both remaining caller rows and remaining estimated compute units.
preparation.why: A response projector should consume the completed admission decision, not invent its own quota policy.
hints: The remaining caller allowance and new batch size must use the same row unit.
The second branch compares compute units, so calculate the batch’s estimated cost before its Threshold gate.

simulation-time-steps.premise: A larger timestep makes a simple cooling simulator generate impossible-looking training trajectories.

construction.title: Expose the numerical update
construction.start: Build the cooling rate from excess temperature, multiply by elapsed step, and update state.
construction.outcome: The source of the overshoot is visible in the arithmetic.
hints: Cooling depends on how far the current temperature is above ambient. Recalculate that excess for the current state.
Turn that excess into a cooling rate, apply the step duration, and update the temperature. A coarse step can cross ambient even though the exact cooling model would approach it without crossing.

investigation.title: The timestep triples
investigation.question: Does the value below ambient establish a new physical effect?
investigation.outcome: Return to a shorter step before training a surrogate on the trajectory.

options.label: No; the coarse Euler step overshoots
options.feedback: The exact model approaches ambient without this crossing from above.

options.label: Yes; the simulator is always ground truth
options.feedback: A numerical approximation can create behaviour absent from the model it approximates.

connections.skill: Interpret a derivative as a local rate
connections.why: We now use that local rate to construct a finite numerical update.

reflection.prompt: What comparison separates numerical error from a wrong cooling law?
reflection.carryForward: Check timestep convergence separately from validation against measured equipment.

simulation-paired-trials.premise: An easier simulated shift made a candidate look better before its policy changed.

construction.title: Pair the policy outcomes
construction.start: Subtract costs on aligned scenarios before taking a mean.
construction.outcome: The comparison describes changes on shared conditions.
hints: Each candidate cost must be compared with the baseline on the same simulated shift. Mixing shifts would mix policy effects with easier conditions.
Keep baseline-minus-candidate gains separate until the final mean. A candidate that costs more on a shift must retain its negative gain.

investigation.title: The unusual shift becomes more expensive
investigation.question: Predict mean gain while keeping the negative gain for the unusual shift.
investigation.outcome: Inspect the regression before deciding whether the average meets the policy requirements.
